questions.question: Trailers built before ____ do not need spring brakes.
questions.explanation: Trailers built before 1975 do not need spring brakes. When you park a trailer without spring brakes, use wheel chocks to stop it from rolling.

questions.question: If you are not sure if a trailer has Anti-Lock Brakes (ABS), you can:

options.text: Look under the trailer for wheel speed sensors near the back of the brakes.
Remove a tire and look for the ABS sensor on the axle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look under the trailer for wheel speed sensors near the back of the brakes.
questions.explanation: If you do not know if a trailer has ABS, look under the vehicle for the control unit and sensor wires near the back of the brakes.

questions.question: When pulling a trailer, the air supply control lever should be in the ____ position.
questions.explanation: Older vehicles may have levers instead of knobs for brake controls. The air supply control should be in the "normal" position when you are pulling a trailer.

questions.question: Fully-loaded trucks:

options.text: Are more likely to roll over than empty trucks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Are more likely to roll over than empty trucks.
questions.explanation: Fully-loaded trucks are more likely to roll over than empty trucks because the heavy cargo raises the center of gravity.

questions.question: Rearward amplification means:

options.text: The amount of noise at the back of a vehicle.
How many trailers a truck can pull.

questions.explanation: Vehicles with trailers can roll over because of the "crack-the-whip" effect, which is caused by rearward amplification.

questions.question: When driving a vehicle with Anti-Lock Brakes (ABS), use the brakes:

options.text: The same way you would in a vehicle without ABS.
While the vehicle is in neutral.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same way you would in a vehicle without ABS.
questions.explanation: When driving a vehicle with ABS, brake the same way you would in a vehicle without ABS.

questions.question: When driving with trailers, you should:

options.text: Press the accelerator all the way down.

questions.explanation: To reduce the risk of rolling over with a trailer, steer gently and smoothly. Avoid sudden movements.

questions.question: Keeping cargo centered on a truck can:
questions.explanation: A rollover is more likely if cargo is unevenly loaded. Keep the load centered on the truck to help prevent rollover.

questions.question: If a parked trailer does not have spring brakes, prevent it from moving by:

options.text: Parking it against a wall or another vehicle.

questions.explanation: If a parked trailer does not have spring brakes, use wheel chocks to keep it from moving.

questions.question: Combination vehicles are usually:

options.text: Easier to drive than single trucks.
Harder to drive than single trucks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Harder to drive than single trucks.
questions.explanation: Combination vehicles require more skill to drive than single trucks. They are longer, heavier, and more likely to roll over.

questions.question: What does the tractor protection valve do?

options.text: It makes sure oil lubricates the engine properly.
It prevents the tractor from going over a set speed.
It keeps air in the truck brake system if the trailer leaks.

questions.correctAnswerText: It keeps air in the truck brake system if the trailer leaks.
questions.explanation: The tractor protection valve keeps air in the tractor or truck brake system if the trailer breaks away or develops a leak. The valve closes automatically if the air pressure drops to an unsafe level.

questions.question: When pulling trailers, what should you do?

options.text: Make sudden turns with the steering wheel.
Push the accelerator all the way down when starting from a stop.

questions.explanation: Always steer gently and smoothly when pulling a trailer. Sudden steering moves can cause the trailer to tip over.

questions.question: How can you best tell if your trailer is skidding?

options.text: By looking at other drivers' faces.
By checking the trailer in your mirrors.

questions.correctAnswerText: By checking the trailer in your mirrors.
questions.explanation: Checking your mirrors is the easiest way to see if your trailer is skidding or jackknifing. You can spot skidding early by watching your trailer in the mirrors.

questions.question: If you must cross traffic with a combination vehicle, what should you do?

options.text: Assume other drivers will make room for your vehicle.
Wait for a gap large enough for your vehicle to safely cross.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for a gap large enough for your vehicle to safely cross.
questions.explanation: Combination vehicles need more space than other vehicles. When entering or crossing traffic, wait for a large enough gap to cross safely.

questions.question: The emergency air line supplies air to the:
questions.explanation: The emergency air line (also called the supply line) does two things. It supplies air to the trailer air tanks and controls the emergency brakes on combination vehicles.

questions.question: When testing ____, apply your vehicle's brakes with the hand control while moving slowly forward.
questions.explanation: To test the trailer service brakes, make sure the brake system has normal air pressure and release the parking brake. Move forward slowly and apply the brakes with the hand control. If working properly, you will feel the brakes activate.

questions.question: Which trailer is most likely to turn over if you turn too quickly?
questions.explanation: Steer gently and smoothly when turning while pulling trailers. Quick turns are dangerous and can cause the last trailer to roll over.

questions.question: When coupling, you should:

options.text: Couple the correct glad hands together.
Couple only one set of glad hands.

questions.correctAnswerText: Couple the correct glad hands together.
questions.explanation: When coupling air brake hoses, connect the correct pairs of glad hands. They are sometimes color-coded to help you avoid mistakes. Blue is usually for service lines and red is usually for emergency lines.

questions.question: When backing a trailer, which direction should you first turn the steering wheel?

options.text: In the direction you want the trailer to go.
In the opposite direction of where you want the trailer to go.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the opposite direction of where you want the trailer to go.
questions.explanation: When backing without a trailer, turn the wheel in the direction you want to go. When backing with a trailer, start by turning in the opposite direction. Once the trailer turns, turn the wheel the other way to follow the trailer.

questions.question: Combination vehicles:

options.text: Often have taller trailers than single commercial vehicles.
Are usually lighter than single commercial vehicles.
Require more skill to drive than single commercial vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Require more skill to drive than single commercial vehicles.
questions.explanation: Driving combination vehicles requires more skill than single commercial vehicles. They are longer, heavier, and more likely to roll over.
